subject: general
question:
Which of the following is / are NOT related to the phenomenon of the universal law of gravitation?

(A) The motion of the moon around the earth.

(B) The tides caused by the moon.

(C) The motion of electrons around the nucleus.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only (C)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Universal Law of Gravitation** states that every mass attracts every other mass in the universe, and the force between two masses is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• The **motion of the moon around the earth** is governed by gravitational forces. The earth exerts a gravitational pull on the moon, keeping it in orbit.
 
• The **tides caused by the moon** are a result of the gravitational pull of the moon on the earth's water bodies, causing tidal bulges.
 
• The **motion of an electron around the nucleus** in an atom is governed by electromagnetic forces, not gravitational forces. Hence, it is not related to the phenomenon of the universal law of gravitation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Motion of the Moon around the Earth**__

 __
 
• The moon is kept in its orbit by the gravitational pull of the earth.
 
• This gravitational force is a perfect example of the universal law of gravitation in action.
 
 
 
• **Tides caused by the Moon**__
 __
 
• Tides are caused by the gravitational interaction between the earth and the moon.
 
• The moon's gravity pulls on the earth's oceans, causing the water to bulge out in the direction of the moon.
 
 
 
• **Motion of Electron around the Nucleus**__
 
 
• Electrons are bound to the nucleus by electromagnetic forces, specifically the Coulomb force between the negatively charged electrons and the positively charged protons in the nucleus.
 
• This force is much stronger than gravitational forces at the atomic scale.
